package.question: Does Method M detect that a benchmark was included in a language model's pretraining data more reliably than existing statistical membership tests across four benchmarks, and does it avoid flagging data the model never saw?
package.methods_summary: Method M is a dataset-membership test for content owners. Before release, each document is rephrased several times by an instruction-tuned LLM, each rephrase carrying a text watermark generated with a different secret key. One rephrased version is published and the others are kept private. To test whether a model was trained on the published version, Method M compares the model's perplexity on the public rephrase with the average perplexity of the private rephrases of the same document, using a one-sided paired t-test (largest 5% of differences clipped). Ablations drop the pairing or the watermarking. Baselines are PaCoST and LLM DI.
package.experimental_setup: Watermarked public and private rephrases of TriviaQA, ARC-C, MMLU and GSM8K (1,000 examples each) were generated with Llama3-70B-Instruct. Pythia-1B was continually pretrained on 6.7B tokens of OpenWebText mixed with the public versions; each benchmark appears exactly once and makes up less than 0.001% of the corpus. Every method returns a p-value for the null hypothesis of no membership. False positives are checked on an uncontaminated Pythia-1B and on held-out subsets watermarked with the same public key. The tables report one p-value per cell; no repeated training runs are reported for these results.

results_tables.caption: P-values for detecting test-set contamination in a continually pretrained Pythia-1B model (lower = stronger evidence of membership). For LLM DI, 'same' uses rephrases of the benchmark questions as the validation set and 'different' uses a disjoint set of unseen questions from the same benchmark.
results_tables.notes: Values copied verbatim from the paper's main results table. The original marks p < 0.05 in bold; bolding is not reproduced. Each benchmark subsample (1,000 examples) appears once in a 6.7B-token training corpus.

results_tables.caption: False-positive analysis: Method M p-values when the tested data were NOT in training. 'Uncontaminated' = a pretrained Pythia-1B model never exposed to the watermarked data; 'Contaminated (held-out)' = testing held-out subsets (same distribution and same public watermark key, different examples) on the contaminated Pythia-1B model.
results_tables.notes: High p-values here mean the test did not (falsely) detect membership. 'Abstracts' and 'Blogs' are two additional real-world document collections used in case studies. A further table with five other off-the-shelf LLMs was dropped.

source_passages.text: PaCoST employs a paired t-test that compares model confidence on original and rephrased versions, while LLM DI aggregates multiple membership inference attacks (MIAs) to perform statistical testing.
